title: Is Organic Really Better? Healthy Food or Trendy Scam?
summary: Animated explainer concluding organic food is not clearly healthier or greener: slightly more antioxidants and fewer residues, but more land and similar emissions.

assertions.quote: several studies found that organic foods contain more antioxidants
the mixed evidence suggests that there are only small differences in nutritional value
it doesn't look like organic food has significant health benefits
Eating veggies is more important for your health than how they were produced.
several studies show that there actually is less pesticide residue on organic produce
Less pesticide does not mean none at all.
Organic pesticides are not necessarily safer than conventional ones.
The study was criticized a lot though.
The pesticides on your vegetables are nothing to lose sleep over.
No production method is clearly better for the environment.
need much more land to produce the same amount of crop

verdicts.note: Meta-analysis of within-publication LCA pairs found organic systems need 25-110% more land per unit of food (p<0.001, n=37), driven by mismatched manure nutrient release and lower yields; mostly high-input Europe/North America systems.

assertions.quote: Organic systems use less energy than conventional ones, but have similar greenhouse gas emissions.

verdicts.note: Per unit of food, organic and conventional greenhouse gas emissions did not differ significantly (4% lower in organic, p=0.59, n=44), because manure N2O offsets savings from avoiding synthetic fertilizer; cradle-to-farm-gate, mostly industrialized systems.
